general_information.Description: Objectives: This course cultivates a comprehensive skillset for students aspiring to thrive in the dynamic field of tour operations. Graduates will emerge proficient in crafting compelling itineraries, implementing effective marketing and sales strategies, and navigating the intricacies of financial management and risk mitigation. Furthermore, the course fosters the development of critical thinking and problem-solving abilities, alongside strong communication skills and a commitment to ethical conduct – all essential for a flourishing career in the ever-evolving tourism industry. Description: This course provides a comprehensive introduction to tour operations and management. Students will gain a thorough understanding of the key concepts and practical skills involved in crafting, organizing, and executing successful tours for travelers.
general_information.StudentTasks: - Class attendance is strongly encouraged. Attend at least 80% of contact hours in order to be accepted to the final examination - Actively participate in class activities - Fulfill tasks given by the instructor after class - Use laptop in class only for learning purposes - Read the textbook in advance - Access the course website (http://flm.fpt.edu.vn) for up-to-date information and material of the course, for online support from teachers and other students, and for practicing and assessment.

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: To articulate the core principles and evolving landscape of tour management within the tourism industry (combines concepts, roles, importance & trends).
Craft comprehensive tour itineraries through a strategic selection of destinations, transportation, accommodation, dining, and sightseeing experiences.
Employ effective sales techniques to captivate potential clients in tourism industry
Deliver exceptional customer service by adeptly handling feedback and resolving complaints with professionalism.
Master tour budgeting, cost management, and cash flow control to ensure financial viability.
Develop superior communication and problem-solving skills to navigate tour operations effectively.
Think critically and adapt by proposing creative solutions to unforeseen challenges and making decisive actions during tours.

assessments.Grading Guide: Participation grade will be given based on students' preparation, and quantity as well as quality of participation in classroom; quality of participation is demonstrated through asking relevant questions, making statements that add to and facilitate class discussion, and builds upon others’ comments. Class preparation and pre-reading before lecture will be assessed upon individuals' understanding and ability to answer questions in the class. Individuals will be called up randomly to be assessed.

assessments.Knowledge and Skill: All knowledge which belong to every single block.
assessments.Note: Instruction and shedules for Quiz must be presented in the Course Implementation Plan approved by director of the campus.Quiz must be taken right after the last lecture of required material.

assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Practical knowledge of real situation Research, problem-solving, planning skills, financial analysis, marketing plan, human resources management, crisis management
assessments.Grading Guide: 1/ Students are required to complete a practical project that they have self-designed (based on what student got from tour project presentation 1 & 2) as part of the practical assessment, which is based on the requirements of the lecturer. All point components of the practical project will be evaluated by lectures of the faculty as well as industry specialists. Should students choose to go the practical way, the evaluation will be based on totally the activities of students in tour, which guided in the "evaluation of Tour practical form." 2/ If students do not want to have Tour project practical, they can choose "Tour project report" instead, the written report is the detailed project version. - The written report should be typed and double-spaced with 11-point font, and can be submitted in soft copy. A deduction of 10% of the assignment mark will be applied for each day of late submission - A 0 (zero) mark will be given to any form of plagiarism detected.

assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Chapters covered in accordance to the lecture of the weeks
assessments.Grading Guide: - Students must work in groups (5-6 students/ group) to figure out basic content for a practical tour that they will submit to their instructor. - The student's presentation content in the first session must include several key elements such as: 1/ Students need to comprehend what type of tour they wish to construct (for example: sightseeing tour, green tourism, eco-tourism, etc.), students must also examine which market will be suitable for the tour (use market analysis models such as Pestel, micro environment, macro environment, etc) 2/ Students must submit general tour information (e.g, outbound or inbound, total trip cost, packages/combos/travel products included). Furthermore, in this part, students might include a sample brochure explaining their tour to boost its vividness and appeal. - After groups have finished presenting, the lecturer should provide relevant comments so that student groups can benefit from their experiences and be prepared to go on to the next stages.
assessments.Note: The tour project must be guided by the instructor during the first lecture. Students will work in team of 5-6 students; The marking will be based on the application of the theory, the understanding of the potential customer and situation and ability to meet their requirements, the ability to analyse situations, develop and evaluate plans Evaluation will be based on the presentation only

assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Chapters covered in accordance to the lecture of the weeks
assessments.Grading Guide: - In this section, after obtaining crucial feedback from the lecturer in Part 1, student groups continue to learn and deliver the remaining content of a full tour. - Student groups must present valuable knowledge as well as an in-depth study of a variety of essential elements in a tour program, including: 1. General information (trip name, type of tour, destination, duration, number of guests, price) 2/ Tour itinerary (detailed daily schedule, accommodation, transport, tourist attractions, experiential activities, meals, tour guide) 3/ Tour cost estimate (travel, hotel, sightseeing, food, operational, and other charges) 4) Tour marketing and communication plan (marketing channels, target customers, pricing strategy, promotion plan) 5/ Risk assessment and solutions (unnoticed risks, treatment options)
